newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel goes global with CC-Amatil deal.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel goes global with CC-Amatil deal.

text.p: Food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp announced plans on Thursday to merge its bottling unit with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd, a move analysts said would propel its soft drinks operations into overseas markets.

Already a player abroad in countries like China through its beer-making operations, the merger of San Miguel's majority-owned Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc with Coca-Cola Co affiliate C-C Amatil dramatically diversifies its soft drinks interests as well.

"It will mean better revenues for San Miguel, which is also expanding its beer operations abroad. It will indeed expose San Miguel to larger markets aside from the Philippines," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities.
The merger of the companies, which would involve the issue of 293 million shares by C-C Amatil worth about $2.7 billion, will create the biggest Coca-Cola bottling group outside the United States.
San Miguel will be the merged company's second biggest stockholder with a 25 percent stake, with Coca-Cola retaining majority ownership at 33 percent.
While analysts lauded the deal, shares of San Miguel failed to sustain initial gains on Thursday in the face of a sharply weaker Manila stock market.
San Miguel's A stock closed unchanged at 55 pesos, while its more indicative B stock ended off 1.50 pesos to 90 after rising to as high as 92 pesos. The Manila index slumped 1.82 percent.
"Definitely, it will benefit San Miguel. It would mean equity income for the company. They can sit back and watch their money come in," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc.

Under the proposal, Coca-Cola Bottlers, which is 70 percent owned by San Miguel, would become a wholly owned subsidiary of Coca-Cola Amatil. Coke has 75 percent share of the soft drinks market in the Philippines.
In a statement on Thursday, San Miguel chief executive officer Andres Soriano III said the transaction "offers San Miguel a magnificent opportunity to advance its internationalisation program."
"The potential synergy will be positive for both San Miguel and Coke. There will be some economies of scale," added Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
